rounds.text: Trigyn Technologies Ltd trades at an extraordinarily low price-to-book ratio of 0.20x on a book value of ₹ 259 with a share price of ₹ 53.0 [E2], representing a severe valuation discount when compared against the sector benchmark P/B of 2.04x [E7]. This massive disconnect is further underscored by a modest P/E of 15 [E1], which sits attractively below the sector benchmark P/E of 21.34x [E6]. Operational momentum has aggressively turned the corner, evidenced by a trailing twelve-month compounded profit growth of 1352% [E21] and a 14% compounded sales growth over the same period [E17]. This stunning acceleration has triggered positive screens, with profit growth exceeding one-year price growth by 1390% as the company begins to outperform expectations [E58]. Conceded: the company has delivered poor compounded sales growth of -8% over 3 years [E16], compounded profit growth of -61% over 3 years [E20], and a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4].

The bull case resting on a seemingly cheap price-to-book ratio of 0.20x [E2] or 0.21x against a sector benchmark of 2.04x [E7] masks a severe, long-term destruction of shareholder value that explains why the stock languishes at just 30% of its 52-week range [E5]. Compounded profit growth tells a catastrophic story of secular decline, having collapsed by 25% over 10 years [E18], 49% over 5 years [E19], and accelerating downward to a staggering -61% over 3 years [E20]. This terminal profitability erosion is further underscored by a meager Return on Assets of just 1.03%, which severely lags the sector benchmark of 5.46% [E8]. Top-line stagnation reinforces this fundamental weakness, as compounded sales growth has stalled at 0% over 5 years [E15] and contracted by -8% over 3 years [E16], compounded by a flagged poor sales growth of -0.18% over the past five years [E63]. Furthermore, shareholders receive zero compensation for enduring this prolonged stagnation and capital destruction, as the dividend yield sits firmly at 0.00% [E4]. Conceded: the company has posted a recent TTM sales growth of 14% [E17] alongside a TTM profit growth spike of 1352% [E21], which temporarily outpaces the 1-year price growth [E58].

Conceded: compounded profit growth over 10 years is -25% [E18], over 5 years is -49% [E19], over 3 years is -61% [E20], and compounded sales growth over 5 years is 0% [E15] with a -8% contraction over 3 years [E16]. However, the bear's focus on past decline completely ignores a dramatic fundamental inflection where trailing twelve-month profit growth has exploded by 1352% [E21] and sales have grown by 14% [E17]. This massive recent acceleration has driven profit growth to exceed 1-year price growth by 1390%, signaling that the company is starting to outperform expectations [E58] rather than continuing a secular terminal decline. Furthermore, dismissing the extreme asset discount of a price-to-book ratio of 0.20x [E2]—trading at a tenth of the sector benchmark of 2.04x [E7]—ignores the immense margin of safety provided against a market capitalization of just ₹ 163 Cr [E3]. Conceded: the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4] and the 5-year sales growth was flagged as poor [E63], but the current valuation ignores a positive screen for profit growth exceeding 20% YoY [E69] and sales growth of 13% YoY [E67] matching the sector median sales growth of 14.0% [E79].
